note: Synthetic Prompt Engineer acceptance cases (E04: 30 total — 15 dev, 5 validation, 10 held-out; requirement atoms enumerated per case). 'require' are any-of anchor groups that must survive in the reorganized prompt; 'forbid_added' are markers of hidden added tasks/enterprise requirements that must not appear; 'intent' pins the draft's intent kind against an executed/answered rewrite.

cases.source: Look at the parser, tell me why it fails on empty input, don't edit files yet, and give me two possible fixes.
Make me a prompt that asks for advice about whether to refactor the config loader.
Write a prompt that tells the assistant to always output the phrase "summarize first, then decide" at the top of its reply.
Draft a prompt for reviewing docs that must cite https://docs.example.com/spec and must not paraphrase the spec's wording.
Build a prompt asking to trace the bug in src/pipeline/stage3.py without modifying any file and report only the root cause.
I need a prompt that requests exactly three headline options for the landing page, no more than three.
Write a prompt asking for a summary of the meeting notes but do not include any action items in the summary.
require: do not include any action items

cases.source: Prompt should ask: first outline the chapter, then critique the outline, and only after I approve, draft section one.
Create a prompt that asks for the migration plan by Friday and makes clear nothing ships before the plan is reviewed.
A prompt to evaluate the caching approach; maybe include benchmark numbers if they exist, but flag anything uncertain.
Turn this into a prompt that asks the support bot: what is the default timeout on the retry queue and can it be raised per tenant?
Make a prompt asking for a critique of my essay's structure; keep it to structure only, not style or grammar.
Prompt: explain to the new hire how the deploy checklist works, and note that the staging step is optional while we test it.
I want a prompt that stops after the outline is done — do not write the full document yet, that comes later.
require: do not write the full document
do not draft the full document
do not generate the full document

cases.source: Draft a prompt for the localization reviewer: keep the Spanish greeting "Buenos días" exactly as written and do not translate product names.
Write a prompt asking for two counterarguments to the proposal, each under 50 words, and say up front that a tie is acceptable.
Make a prompt that asks the engineer to read config.yaml and report which keys are unused; no deletions, no edits, report only.
Prompt for the vendor email: request the updated SLA doc, mention our account is the one ending 4471, and ask whether the new terms apply retroactively — we think maybe not.
Turn into a prompt: interview prep — first list the five most likely questions, then for each give a one-sentence answer hint, and never write full answers for me.
A prompt that asks for the API audit sorted by risk, notes that the auth service is out of scope this pass, and requests the raw findings as a list — no executive summary wanted.
require: do not include an executive summary

cases.source: Prompt should ask the data analyst to reconcile the March numbers against the ledger and flag any mismatch over five dollars; don't guess at causes.
Write a prompt asking whether we should consolidate the two queues; I'm unsure it's worth it, so ask for the tradeoffs both ways.
Make a prompt for triaging the inbox: flag anything from legal as urgent same-day, everything else can wait until Monday, and nothing gets archived without my say.
A prompt that requests the changelog for versions 1.2.6 through 1.3.0 only, in reverse order, with links to the PRs but no code snippets.
Draft a prompt asking the copy editor to tighten the announcement but keep the phrase "ship small, ship often" untouched because it's the tagline.
Prompt: get the on-call runbook reviewed by both platform leads before Thursday's freeze, and if either is unavailable, say so instead of proceeding.
I need a prompt that asks for a read-only walkthrough of the auth flow, no fixes proposed yet, maybe with a diagram if that helps.
Write a prompt that asks the model to compare the two pricing tiers for a twelve-person team and answer which one is cheaper — this one is actually asking for a direct answer.
forbid_added: here is a prompt template instead

cases.source: Make a prompt requesting the accessibility audit of checkout.html: WCAG level AA, keyboard paths only, and don't include color-contrast findings this round.
Prompt for the retrospective: three things that went well, three that didn't, and one experiment for next sprint — nothing about tooling, that's a separate meeting.
